name: Wild Mustard

facts.how: Leaves cooked; flowers raw; seeds as mustard
facts.where: Fields and roadsides, often in yellow sheets
facts.value: Vitamins A and C; the seeds make mustard

caution: A safe mustard-family plant; harvest young leaves away from sprayed fields. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Fields of four-petaled yellow flowers in early spring; every mustard has flowers in a cross of four petals and a peppery bite.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Young leaves cook into mustard greens; the bright flowers dress a salad, and the ground seeds are literally mustard.
